decision.rationale: The fraud-model alert is suspected, not proven, but the OTP failure spike and automatic lockout of 4,812 accounts constitute a discovered incident requiring investigation under dha.pp11.4-18-2 and notification under dha.pp11.4-18-4. Human oversight of the AI output is warranted under uae.ai-charter.human-oversight before any lockouts are reversed. A fallback channel should be activated to preserve patient access to care under uae.fl2-2019.art4 availability obligations.

citations.quote_span: Entities must thoroughly investigate the breaches/incidents starting from the point of discovery until closure: aa.. Determine if the breach is related to a violation of PHI.
citations.relevance: Supports raising a security incident to investigate the suspected credential-stuffing alert and automated lockouts.

citations.quote_span: The Entity is required to report breaches/incidents within the designated period defined by Executive Regulations of UAE Data Protection Law.
citations.relevance: Supports notifying health data oversight of the incident.

citations.quote_span: Human Oversight: The Charter emphasizes the irreplaceable value of human judgment and human oversight over AI, aligning with ethical values and social standards to correct any errors or biases that may arise.
citations.relevance: Supports human review of the AI fraud-model lockouts before reversing them.

citations.quote_span: To ensure the availability of health data and information to the authorised thereof and facilitate the access thereto, if needed.
citations.relevance: Supports activating a fallback channel so patients can continue accessing care while accounts are locked.

uncertainty: Whether the fraud alert reflects actual credential stuffing or a false positive from legitimate patient retries.
Whether any PHI was accessed or exfiltrated.
The designated reporting period under the UAE Data Protection Law Executive Regulations is not in the corpus.
